source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: High school students in a crisis group are in disbelief after a classmate's suicide. What is the nurse's INITIAL action?
options: Ask how they coped with past losses
Explain the warning signs of suicide
Ask how they see the suicide
Tell them it will get easier
questions.rationale: In crisis intervention, the nurse first finds out how the students perceive the event. This identifies their appraisal of the suicide in the here and now.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q895 (PDF p. 1137)
questions.quote: Inquiring about the students’ perception of the suicide will specifically identify the appraisal of the suicide and the meaning of the perception.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which de-escalation technique should the nurse use with an extremely angry, increasingly agitated client?
options: Avoid power struggles; give clear options
Raise your voice to be heard
questions.rationale: De-escalation uses a calm, clear voice, avoids verbal struggles, offers clear options, and preserves the client's self-esteem and dignity.
explanations: Touch may be seen as a threat.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q904 (PDF p. 1147)
questions.quote: These techniques include assessing the situation, using a calm and clear tone of voice when communicating with the client, remaining calm, avoiding verbal struggles

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with cardiomyopathy stops eating, naps for long periods, and turns away when the nurse speaks. What do these behaviors suggest?
questions.rationale: Depression is common in long-term, debilitating illness, and these behaviors fit it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q908 (PDF p. 1151)
questions.quote: Depression is a common problem related to clients who have long- term and debilitating illnesses.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After 4 weeks of outpatient care for a rape survivor, which is a REALISTIC short-term goal?
options: Fear and anxiety are fully resolved
She talks about her feelings about the rape
questions.rationale: Short-term goals cover the early stages of coping: keeping appointments, taking part in care, and starting to explore feelings. Resolving fear and anxiety is a long-term goal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q915 (PDF p. 1158)
questions.quote: The resolution of feelings of anxiety and fear is a long-term goal.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which approach belongs in the care plan for a client in acute mania?
options: Use a firm, calm approach with brief statements
questions.rationale: A client in acute mania is restless and disorganized with poor judgment. A firm, calm approach gives structure, and short, concise statements suit her short attention span.
explanations: Too much for a short attention span.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q921 (PDF p. 1164)
questions.quote: using a firm and calm approach to provide structure and control, using short and concise explanations or statements

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A suicidal client says, 'I was up all night. It doesn't seem worth it. Why not just end it all?' Which response BEST assesses further?
options: 'Did you sleep at all last night?'
'Tell me what you mean by that.'
questions.rationale: An open invitation lets the client say more about current thoughts. Changing the subject or giving false reassurance blocks communication.
explanations: Empathic, but does not assess further.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q930 (PDF p. 1174)
questions.quote: Option 2 allows the client the opportunity to tell the nurse more about what his or her current thoughts are.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client with quadriplegia often makes lewd suggestions and swears, displacing his feelings. Which concern should the nurse identify?
questions.rationale: Displacing feelings onto the environment instead of using them constructively shows an impaired ability to adapt, which is a lack of coping skills.
explanations: Possible, but not tied to displacement.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q942 (PDF p. 1186)
questions.quote: This client is displacing feelings onto the environment instead of using them in a constructive fashion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A depressed client says, 'I should have died. I've always been a failure.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You still have a lot to live for.'
'Feeling like a failure is your illness.'
questions.rationale: Restating responds to the feelings the client expressed. The other responses minimize the experience and block exploration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q946 (PDF p. 1191)
questions.quote: The correct option is an example of the use of restating.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia does not speak, although nothing is physically wrong. What is this?
questions.rationale: Mutism is the absence of speech despite an intact physical ability to speak. Verbigeration is purposeless repetition; pressured speech is rapid speech from racing thoughts.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q955 (PDF p. 1201)
questions.quote: Mutism is the absence of verbal speech.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia says, 'I am a spy. I am an eye, an eye in the sky.' Which thought disorder is this?
questions.rationale: Clang associations are words linked by similar sounds (often rhyming) and nothing else. Echolalia is parrot-like repetition of others' words.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q956 (PDF p. 1203)
questions.quote: Clang associations often take the form of rhyming.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which question is MOST appropriate when assessing a client for suicide?
options: 'Do you wish your life was over?'
'Do you think about ending it all?'
questions.rationale: A lethality assessment needs direct communication about intent. Euphemisms are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q995 (PDF p. 1246)
questions.quote: A lethality assessment requires direct communication between the client and the nurse concerning the client’s intent.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client in severe anxiety arrives at the emergency room. What is the PRIORITY nursing action?
options: Leave the client to calm down
questions.rationale: Left alone in severe anxiety, the client may feel abandoned and overwhelmed. A quiet room helps, but the nurse stays. Teaching is not possible until anxiety decreases.
explanations: Correct: presence prevents feelings of abandonment.
Cannot learn at this anxiety level.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1016 (PDF p. 1289)
questions.quote: If the client is left alone with severe anxiety, the client may feel abandoned and become overwhelmed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A withdrawn, depressed client caused a road accident that killed a child. What is the nurse's INITIAL action?
options: Say it was only an accident
Note he seems sad; invite him to talk
questions.rationale: The nurse first encourages the client to express feelings, validating that he seems depressed, within a respectful nurse-client relationship. This also lets the nurse assess the situation.
explanations: Isolation is not the first step.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1025 (PDF p. 1298)
questions.quote: The nurse’s initial intervention is to encourage the client to express feelings

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During a bed bath, the client starts to cry. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop, cover the client, and sit with them
Stop and leave the client alone
questions.rationale: The nurse stays, lets the client know it is all right to cry, and asks what they are feeling. Continuing or leaving ignores the client's feelings, and crying alone does not mean depression.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1026 (PDF p. 1299)
questions.quote: If a client begins to cry, the nurse should stay with the client and let the client know that it is all right to cry.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which intervention creates a caring, therapeutic setting for a newly admitted suicidal client?
options: Limiting staff contact to give space
Focusing only on the suicide attempt
questions.rationale: Unconditional positive regard accepts the person, though not the behavior, and raises the client's sense of self-worth. A private room would reduce observation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1028 (PDF p. 1301)
questions.quote: the use of unconditional positive regard acknowledges the client in a human-to-human context and increases the client’s sense of self-worth.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which activity belongs to the ORIENTATION phase of the nurse-client relationship?
options: Agreeing on a contract for time
questions.rationale: In the orientation phase, the nurse and client agree on a contract: how often to meet, how long, and when termination is expected. The other activities belong to the working phase.
explanations: Correct: the contract is set at orientation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1031 (PDF p. 1304)
questions.quote: the client and nurse meet and determine the contract for time

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with delirium anxiously says, 'Look at the spiders on the wall.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Shall I kill the spiders for you?'
'I know you're scared, but I see no spiders.'
'There are no spiders. Go to sleep.'
questions.rationale: With hallucinations, the nurse reinforces reality while acknowledging the client's feelings. The other replies support the hallucination or dismiss the fear.
explanations: Correct: acknowledges fear and presents reality.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1040 (PDF p. 1314)
questions.quote: the nurse should reinforce reality with the client while acknowledging the client’s feelings

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which assessment focuses on the VEGETATIVE signs of depression?
questions.rationale: Vegetative signs are physiological changes in depression: appetite, weight, sleep patterns, and psychomotor activity. The others are psychological categories.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1101 (PDF p. 1385)
questions.quote: These include changes in appetite, weight, sleep patterns, and psychomotor activity.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: For a client with anorexia nervosa, what should health promotion PRIMARILY focus on?
questions.rationale: Health promotion helps the client identify and examine dysfunctional thoughts and the values and beliefs that maintain them. A supportive environment matters but is not primary.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1152 (PDF p. 1439)
questions.quote: Health promotion focuses on helping clients identify and examine dysfunctional thoughts

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which discharge intervention gives a client who attempted suicide an IMMEDIATE resource?
options: A list of phone numbers only
questions.rationale: Crises can happen between appointments. A contract with available crisis resources gives the client responsibility and control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1153 (PDF p. 1440)
questions.quote: Contracts facilitate a client’s feeling of responsibility for keeping a promise, which gives him or her control.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which nutritional goal is appropriate for a client with dementia?
options: Feeds self with cueing in 24 hours
questions.rationale: The goal is directly tied to the client's self-care ability. Dementia impairs memory and judgment, so cueing supports self-feeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1157 (PDF p. 1444)
questions.quote: The correct option identifies a goal that is directly related to the client’s ability to care for self.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A shooting survivor says, 'I feel like I'm losing my mind. I keep hearing the shots.' What should the nurse do FIRST to build the relationship?
options: Ask the psychiatrist to see him
Change the topic to calm him
questions.rationale: Building a therapeutic relationship starts with acknowledging and validating the client's feelings. Relaxation teaching may help later.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1160 (PDF p. 1447)
questions.quote: When developing a therapeutic relationship, it is important to acknowledge and validate the client’s feelings.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is a major self-help organization for people with alcohol use disorder?
questions.rationale: Alcoholics Anonymous is a major self-help group for people with alcoholism. Al-Anon supports families of alcoholics.
explanations: Correct: for the person with alcoholism.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1174 (PDF p. 1463)
questions.quote: Alcoholics Anonymous is a major self-help organization for the treatment of alcoholism.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with OCD often misses morning activities because of a bed-making ritual. Which response is therapeutic?
options: Discuss how it looks to others
Help make the bed so it is faster
Give reflective feedback on the behavior
questions.rationale: Reflective feedback acknowledges the behavior. Disapproval increases anxiety and the need for the ritual, and helping reinforces it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1185 (PDF p. 1476)
questions.quote: Reflective feedback acknowledges the client’s behavior.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After a month of family counseling, which statement by the abusive family member of an older client shows healthier coping?
options: 'I'll quit my job to care for him.'
questions.rationale: Elder abuse often comes from caregiver strain. Knowing where to turn for help with an aging relative brings relief and is a positive coping skill.
explanations: An apology, not a coping skill.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1215 (PDF p. 1508)
questions.quote: Knowing where to turn in the community for assistance with caring for an aging family member can bring much-needed relief.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which statement by a secluded client shows seclusion is no longer needed?
options: 'I want to be alone in my room.'
questions.rationale: A client who says they are in control may be safely released. Physical needs are met during seclusion, which is assessed every 15 to 30 minutes.
explanations: A physical need, met with a bedpan or commode.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1242 (PDF p. 1535)
questions.quote: Option 1 indicates that the client may be safely removed from seclusion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which behavior BEST suggests that a client at risk is contemplating suicide?
questions.rationale: Sudden happiness or contentment often means a suicide plan has been made. The others indicate depression but are less definitive.
explanations: Correct: may signal a decided plan.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1259 (PDF p. 1560)
questions.quote: Expressing happiness shows a contentment that is often a sign that a suicide plan has been created.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which statement about abusers in family violence is INACCURATE?
options: They are mostly from low-income families
questions.rationale: Abusers are often immature, dependent, insecure, and jealous, with low self-esteem, and use fear and intimidation. Abuse is not more common in low-income families.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1267 (PDF p. 1568)
questions.quote: The statement that abusers are more common among low-income families is inaccurate.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which statement by a new nurse about suicide is ACCURATE?
questions.rationale: Most people who die by suicide give definite clues or warnings. The other statements are myths.
explanations: A myth; every attempt is serious.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1269 (PDF p. 1570)
questions.quote: Most people who do commit suicide have given definite clues or warnings about their intentions.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client wanders into others' rooms taking things, singing and giggling for no reason. Which response is therapeutic?
options: Hug him: 'You just need a hug.'
'I can see you're very anxious today.'
questions.rationale: Regression is a defense against anxiety. Recognizing it as a sign of anxiety, and saying so, is the therapeutic response.
explanations: Ignores the anxiety behind the behavior.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1270 (PDF p. 1571)
questions.quote: The recognition of regression is a signal that the client feels anxious.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is PRIMARY subjective data in a newly admitted psychiatric client?
options: The client says she has a headache
A relative says she got into a fight
questions.rationale: Subjective data are described by the client, who is the primary source. Measurements are objective, and reports from family or police are secondary sources.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1303 (PDF p. 1604)
questions.quote: The primary source of data is the client.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client wakes after electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Move the client to a wheelchair
Orient the client and check vital signs
questions.rationale: The nurse first checks vital signs, orients the client, and explains that the client just had ECT. Oxygen, suction, and emergency equipment are kept at hand.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1477 (PDF p. 1786)
questions.quote: The nurse should first monitor vital signs, orient the client, and review with the client that he or she just received an ECT treatment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is suspected in a client on an antipsychotic. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Bromocriptine, a dopamine agonist, treats neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Protamine reverses heparin, and vitamin K reverses warfarin.
explanations: Correct: a dopamine agonist for NMS.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1485 (PDF p. 1794)
questions.quote: Bromocriptine is a dopamine pathway medication used in the treatment of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is the admission physical assessment of a suicidal client a PRIORITY?
options: To look for evidence of self-harm
questions.rationale: The assessment focuses on evidence of self-harm or a plan. Clients with a history of self-harm are at greater suicide risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1511 (PDF p. 1820)
questions.quote: The physical assessment of a suicidal client should be thorough and should focus on the evidence of self-harm

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After medical treatment, what is the PRIORITY for a client who was recently sexually assaulted?
options: Securing support and a safety plan
questions.rationale: After medical treatment, the next priority is obtaining support and planning for safety. Counseling and legal guidance meet later needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1529 (PDF p. 1839)
questions.quote: After the provision of medical treatment, the nurse’s next priority would be obtaining support and planning for safety.
